title: Agent reply
description: Every reply is exactly ONE JSON object, in one of two shapes. (1) A context request, {"observe": [...]}, when you need to look at the project before you can propose: the runtime shows you what you asked for and asks again. (2) A proposal, {"intents": [...]}, when you have what you need: it ends the exchange. Never both in one reply, and no other top-level keys. Every path in it is relative to the project root. See docs/wire_schema.md for the human-readable version of this same contract -- keep the two in sync.

proposal.description: Your final answer: the complete work you propose. Send it only once you have seen what you need -- if you still need to look at the project, send a context request instead. A read_file, glob or grep inside a proposal is part of the proposed work (for example the evidence a claim cites); it is not a way to look at the project.

intents.description: The proposed work, in order. Every intent needed to carry it out.

context_request.description: Send this INSTEAD of a proposal when you need to see files before you can propose: a list of observations. The runtime makes each one, read-only, and asks you again with the results; nothing is changed and nothing is proposed. The whole reply is this one object.

observation.description: One thing to look at before proposing, and why. Wraps a single read-only intent. The runtime records each observation with the proposal it leads to, together with what you were shown.

reason.description: Why you need to see this, in one short sentence. Kept on record with the proposal.

observation_intent.description: The intent an observation wraps: a read_file, glob or grep, with exactly the fields that intent has in a proposal. No other intent type is allowed here.

ref.description: Arbitrary caller-chosen name for this intent, resolvable later via a claim's evidence.source_intent_ref. Meaningful only within this one response, and must be unique within it.

path.description: Relative to the project root, e.g. "lib/signup.ex". Must not contain ".." and must stay inside the project.

write_file.description: Creates a new file. Fails when applied if the file already exists -- change an existing file with file_patch.

path.description: Relative to the project root, e.g. "lib/signup.ex". Must not contain ".." and must stay inside the project.

contents.description: The complete contents of the new file.

Relative to the project root, e.g. "lib/signup.ex". Must not contain ".." and must stay inside the project.

diff.description: A unified diff of this one file -- the format `diff -u` produces -- applied with exactly `patch --batch --forward --fuzz=0 <path> <diff>`. Hunk headers ("@@ -old_start,old_count +new_start,new_count @@") need exact line counts, and context and removed lines must match the current file exactly. The ---/+++ file names are ignored; the target is `path`. Other patch formats (e.g. "*** Begin Patch") are rejected.

cmd.description: An executable name, run in the project root with `args`. Not a shell: no pipes, redirects or globbing.

pattern.description: A literal string, matched line by line. Not a regular expression.

paths.description: Files to search. Directories are not searched; list files (find them with glob).

items.description: Relative to the project root, e.g. "lib/signup.ex". Must not contain ".." and must stay inside the project.

base_dir.description: Relative to the project root, e.g. "lib/signup.ex". Must not contain ".." and must stay inside the project. Defaults to ".".
